Put the memory structures back.

Place the left hippocampus, left amygdala and left thalamus into their anatomically grounded positions. Their contours and relative positions come from your uploaded BodyParts3D meshes. The flat view is a teaching projection, not a full brain reconstruction.

Great work. These are three distinct left-hemisphere structures. Their relative positions are derived from the source models; this projection is not a single anatomical slice.

What is anatomically accurate here?

The colored shapes are projections of the actual user-supplied BodyParts3D OBJ meshes for FJ1759 (left hippocampus), FJ1753 (left amygdala), and FJ1782 (left thalamus). Projection preserves the shared source coordinate system in the Y–Z plane, and target locations are derived from source coordinates. Mesh triangles were sampled in v28 for lightweight web rendering. No surrounding brain tissue, axons or connections are claimed. The teaching projection intentionally does not imply that these structures lie in a single anatomical section.

Scientific limits & licensing

BodyParts3D FJ series, compatibility version 4.0. Each uploaded OBJ explicitly declares “Creative Commons Attribution-Share Alike 2.1 Japan”. Attribution: BodyParts3D, (c) The Database Center for Life Science, licensed under CC Attribution-Share Alike 2.1 Japan. This license has Share-Alike requirements for adaptations. Geometry is surface anatomy only: no neuron-scale layers, axonal connections, or proof of functional pathways. Sampled triangles are used for performance; original OBJ files are retained separately.

Source: BodyParts3D license. Identification uses each uploaded OBJ file's own English name, representation ID, and FMA concept ID.

FROM NEURI’S FIELD NOTES · ENTRY 01

Neuri’s lost message

“I was carrying a memory across the brain, and I got lost. I remember a curved structure, a long cable and a tiny relay… but not the order.”

Each stop teaches where a structure is, what it does, and what happens when it is damaged. No prior knowledge needed.

Neuri is a fictional guide. The anatomy is real and simplified for first-time learners.
